findings.issue_text: [BUG] The permission check ANDs isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner instead of OR-ing them, so a team admin who is not the owner is denied, and the check only passes a team owner (for whom isTeamAdmin is already true), making the admin check dead code. A team admin of the event type's team who is neither the organizer nor an attendee gets a FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission' error when adding guests, defeating the apparent intent to allow admins.

[BUG] renderEmail("AttendeeAddGuestsEmail", ...) and renderEmail("OrganizerAddGuestsEmail", ...) rely on a template-name registry in packages/emails/index.ts that this diff never registers the new components in, so the lookup resolves to undefined and React.createElement(undefined) throws when the handler triggers email sending. Every addGuests call crashes inside sendAddGuestsEmails (caught only by the broad try/catch, so no confirmation emails are ever sent to organizer, attendees, or new guests, silently).

[ADVISORY] The catch block around sendAddGuestsEmails swallows all errors with a bare console.log and no error detail, and the handler still returns success. Users see 'Guests added' success toast even when all notification emails failed; operators debugging missing emails get only the literal string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' with no err object or booking id.

[ADVISORY] The error toast message is built as a template literal `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which is always a non-empty string, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is unreachable and t(err.message) is applied to raw server error strings like 'you_do_not_have_permission' that are not always translation keys. Users see untranslated or code-leaking error toasts (e.g. 'UNAUTHORIZED: booking_not_found' passed through t() verbatim) instead of the intended human message.

[ADVISORY] Every rendered EmailField row plus the outer label shares the same htmlFor/id convention ('emails' label pointing to nothing, keys are indices), and the removal button is wrapped in a Tooltip with the hard-coded untranslated string "Remove email" while every other user-facing string in the component goes through t(). Non-English users get an English tooltip in the add-guests dialog, and screen-reader users get an unlabeled/incorrectly-associated email input list.

[ADVISORY] The new addGuests mutation handler (permission logic, guest dedup, blacklist filtering, attendee creation, calendar update, email fan-out) ships with no test of any kind in this diff, despite the diff adding a data-testid='add_members' clearly intended for e2e coverage. A regression in the permission check or the uniqueGuests filter (e.g. re-adding an existing attendee, adding blacklisted emails) would silently create duplicate Attendee rows or email the wrong people, and nothing in CI would catch it.

[ADVISORY] ZAddGuestsInputSchema is constructed inside the component body, so a new Zod schema object (and Set) is allocated on every render of the booking list item's dialog. Wasted allocation per render across every booking row; minor perf smell, and the schema also silently accepts the single empty-string initial value [''] as length 1 while email() rejects it, producing the isInvalidEmail error banner rather than a graceful 'enter an email' prompt.

[BUG] The team-permission check uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both an admin AND an owner. A team admin who is not the team owner (and not the organizer or an attendee) calling addGuests on a team booking gets a 403 FORBIDDEN, even though admins are clearly intended to manage team bookings; the permission tier is silently narrowed to owners-only.

[BUG] EventManager is constructed with ctx.user's credentials and identity, not the booking organizer's, when a non-organizer attendee adds guests. When an attendee (not the organizer) adds guests, eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs with the attendee's (likely empty) credentials and the attendee's calendars, so the organizer's external calendar (Google/Outlook) attendee list is never updated — the new guests silently never appear on the organizer's calendar event.

[BUG] Guest dedup and blacklist matching are case-sensitive string equality while the blacklist is lowercased. process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is split and lowercased, then compared with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where guest retains original case, so 'User@Example.com' bypasses a 'user@example.com' blacklist entry; likewise a guest differing only in case from an existing attendee is re-created as a duplicate BookingAttendee row.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails branches on the raw input `guests` array rather than the guests actually persisted (`uniqueGuests`), and existing-attendee duplicates and blacklisted emails are not filtered out of that list. An attendee whose email is already on the booking but was re-typed into the input receives a full AttendeeScheduledEmail (a complete 'your booking is confirmed' email) instead of the AddGuests notification, confusing existing participants with a duplicate confirmation.

[BUG] Blacklisted guests are silently dropped rather than rejected, and the handler passes the unfiltered `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails while persisting only uniqueGuests. A user who adds [good@example.com, blacklisted@example.com] sees 'Guests added' with no indication the blacklisted guest was excluded — no acceptance criterion or error message communicates the partial failure, so the user believes the guest was invited.

[ADVISORY] The handler unconditionally loads an env var BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS with no documentation, .env.example entry, or feature flag. Operators cannot discover or configure the guest blacklist without reading source; behavior gating on a raw env var also cannot be disabled/enabled per-instance without a code deploy reference point.

[ADVISORY] The handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees from the event type but never enforces seat capacity when adding guests. On a seat-based event type, an organizer or attendee can add unlimited guests via this endpoint, exceeding seatsPerTimeSlot and producing attendee counts the seats logic elsewhere assumes are bounded — seat-count invariants silently break.

[BUG] prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws an unhandled Prisma NOT_FOUND error when booking.userId is null (e.g. system bookings). A booking with a null userId in the DB makes the addGuests mutation throw a raw Prisma error, returning a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of the 4xx the TRPCError-based contract elsewhere in this handler promises.

[ADVISORY] New guests are persisted with name: "" and organizer's timeZone, and no guest-visible name is ever collected or backfilled. Emails/ICS invites addressed to ' <guest@example.com>' and displayed lists show blank names for added guests; downstream consumers assuming non-empty attendee names render broken rows.

[BUG] The permission gate computes isTeamAdminOrOwner as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), requiring the caller to be BOTH an admin and an owner simultaneously, so plain team admins who are not owners are rejected. A team admin (not owner) who opens the new 'additional_guests' menu item on a team booking gets a 403 'you_do_not_have_permission' — the shipped UI invites them to use a backend that refuses them.

[BUG] Blacklist comparison lowercases BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS but never lowercases the incoming guest email, so `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` never matches a guest submitted with any uppercase character. Operators who configure BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS (e.g. 'DoNotBook@corp.com') to block specific emails get silently bypassed by submitting 'donotbook@CORP.com', and the banned guest is added as an attendee and emailed the booking details.

[BUG] The server schema is a hand-maintained duplicate of the client-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx (lines 30-35) but is missing the .refine() uniqueness check that only the client copy has, so the server accepts duplicate emails. Any API client (or a stale UI bundle) posting {guests: ["a@b.com","a@b.com"]} causes createMany to insert duplicate attendee rows for the same email, and the attendee receives duplicate emails on every subsequent guest-add since the dedupe filter in the handler (line 79) is exact-match per-row and does not collapse within-request duplicates.

[ADVISORY] The handler never validates the resulting attendee count against eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot even though it reads seatsPerTimeSlot into evt (line ~148), so the seats invariant is not enforced by the one code path that can add unbounded attendees. On a seats event with seatsPerTimeSlot=5 and 3 existing attendees, an organizer adds 20 guests; all 23 rows are created with no error, and every future booking-logic branch that assumes attendee count <= seats (waitlists, cancellation of the seat booking) operates on corrupted state.

[ADVISORY] New guests are persisted with name: "", so BookingAttendee rows exist with empty names while every email template and downstream consumer renders attendee.name. Organizer/attendee 'Guests Added' emails and ICS contents show blank names for the added guests, and OrganizerAddGuestsEmail's subject uses attendees[0].name which can render an empty string when the booker was itself an empty-named guest.

[BUG] updateCalendarAttendees is invoked through an EventManager constructed with the CALLING user's credentials (ctx.user), not the booking organizer's, even though the permission gate explicitly allows plain attendees to call this mutation. When an attendee (not the organizer) adds guests, the EventManager has none of the organizer's calendar credentials, so the external calendar event's attendee list is never updated — the new guest is added to the DB and emailed but is absent from the organizer's Google/Outlook event, desynchronizing the source of truth.

[ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw input `guests` array rather than the deduped `uniqueGuests` used for the DB insert, and email failures are swallowed by a bare console.log. When the request contains emails the server deduped (existing attendees or blacklisted entries), the notification decision in sendAddGuestsEmails is computed off a different list than what was written; and operators get no telemetry when the guest-notification emails fail, so a 'Guests added' success toast masks that nobody was notified.

[ADVISORY] The new addGuests mutation — a 174-line handler with authorization, blacklist, dedupe, calendar-sync and email-blast logic — ships with zero tests anywhere in the diff. The permission-gate && vs || defect, the case-sensitive blacklist bypass, and the seats-invariant hole are all regressions no test would have needed creativity to catch; the next refactor of this handler (e.g. touching the attendee filter) ships unverified against the booking list UI contract.

[ADVISORY] A brand-new BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env var is introduced as the only way to disable the guest feature for specific emails, with no feature flag or settings entry, and the guest emails are compared against attendees case-sensitively (`guest === attendee.email`, line 80). An operator who wants to prevent guest-adding cannot turn the menu item off without a code deploy, and a guest whose email differs only in case from an existing attendee ("User@x.com" vs "user@x.com") bypasses the duplicate filter and receives the attendee's duplicate records on the same booking.

[BUG] The team permission check uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner. A team admin who is not the owner of a team booking gets FORBIDDEN when calling addGuests on a booking they should be able to manage; the intended 'admin OR owner' authorization is silently narrowed to the intersection.

[BUG] The blacklist comparison compares raw guest input against lowercased blacklist entries, so any mixed-case email bypasses the blacklist. BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS='bad@x.com' is defeated by submitting 'Bad@x.com' — the equality check guest === blacklisted entry never matches because guests are never lowercased before comparison.

[BUG] The uniqueGuests filter only removes emails already present in booking.attendees and the blacklist, but does not deduplicate duplicates within the guests array itself (the server ZAddGuestsInputSchema has no uniqueness refinement, unlike the client copy in AddGuestsDialog.tsx). A client (or curl) sending guests:["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes server validation and createMany inserts two identical attendee rows for the same booking, sending duplicate invites and corrupting the attendee list; the client-side refine is a stand-in guard that the server endpoint, the real boundary, does not enforce.

[BUG] The EventManager is constructed with ctx.user (the calling user) and that user's credentials, not the booking organizer's, even though any attendee is authorized to call addGuests. When an attendee (not the organizer) adds guests, the calendar update runs with the attendee's credentials — who has no write access to the organizer's calendar event — so updateCalendarAttendees fails or silently updates nothing, while the DB attendees are already mutated, leaving booking.attendees and the external calendar event permanently out of sync.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw input guests instead of uniqueGuests (the list actually added), and newGuests.includes(attendee.email) is case-sensitive against attendee rows. Emails listed in guests that were filtered out (already an attendee or blacklisted) still cause that existing attendee to receive a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail, i.e. a duplicate 'scheduled' email for an event that did not change for them.

[ADVISORY] isAttendee matches only user.email against booking.attendees, so a user whose booking was made under a secondary/changed email is denied, while conversely any previously-added guest (name "", arbitrary email) is granted full add-guest permission. Any guest added to a booking gains the ability to add more guests recursively (no organizer gate on propagation), and organizers with multiple emails hit spurious FORBIDDEN on their own bookings.

[ADVISORY] Guests are unconditionally appended to booking.attendees with no check against eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot, even though seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees are read into the CalendarEvent two lines below. For seat-limited event types, an organizer or attendee can push attendees past the seat limit through this path, overbooking a seats booking; the seat invariant enforced at booking time is not enforced here.

[ADVISORY] List items use array index as the React key while entries are removed via splice, in a component whose only purpose is mutable row editing. Removing a middle email field while typing causes input state and focus to jump to the wrong row on the next render, biting any user managing 3+ emails; a stable id per row is the right data structure for a mutable list.

[BUG] The team-permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`, so it requires the caller to be simultaneously a team admin AND a team owner rather than either. A user who is a team admin but not the owner (or vice versa) gets FORBIDDEN on addGuests for team bookings where they are neither organizer nor attendee — the accepted intent (admins or owners can manage guests) is silently inverted, and since almost no one satisfies both roles the check is effectively dead code granting nothing.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw input `guests` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. When the user submits a mix of new emails and emails already on the booking (which the DB-write path silently filters), sendAddGuestsEmails (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525) sends those already-present attendees the full AttendeeScheduledEmail re-confirmation instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notification — an email-sending objective drift where the same person gets both an 'Added' notice and a spurious 'scheduled' email depending on what else was in the list.

[BUG] The blacklist check lowercases only the blacklist entries but compares them against the guest email as submitted, so the comparison is case-sensitive. A guest email like `User@Blocked.com` bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entirely because `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes('User@Blocked.com')` is false while `user@blocked.com` is in the list — the operator-configured exclusion is trivially defeated by case variation.

[BUG] The dialog state is initialized to `[""]`, so validation always receives at least one empty string even when the user has not typed anything, and `handleAdd` can never hit its `length === 0` early return. Opening the dialog and clicking Add shows the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' error without the user having entered anything, and if the user removes all rows via the x addon (value becomes `[]`), MultiEmail switches to the empty-state button, so the two component states disagree about what an empty form is.

[ADVISORY] The `add_members` menu option is appended unconditionally to every booking's option list, while the server rejects most callers with FORBIDDEN. Non-organizer, non-attendee users (e.g. bookers viewing past bookings or team members) see the 'Additional guests' option, open the dialog, enter emails, click Add, and receive a raw `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission` toast — the UI advertises a capability the endpoint denies.

[ADVISORY] The Dialog's `onOpenChange` path (Esc key, backdrop click, dialog header close) closes the dialog without resetting `multiEmailValue` or `isInvalidEmail`; only the explicit Cancel button resets state. A user who types emails, dismisses via Esc, and reopens the dialog sees the stale entries and any stale error banner from the previous attempt, and stale emails are then submitted on the next Add.

[ADVISORY] New guests are created with `name: ""` and no booking confirmation of their own outside the email path, and sendAddGuestsEmails failures are swallowed with a bare `console.log`. If email delivery fails, guests are persisted as attendees with blank names on the booking (and on the calendar invite via updateCalendarAttendees) but never notified, with no error surfaced to the caller and no retry — the operator sees 'Guests added' success while the guest has no way to know they were invited.

[BUG] The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS deny list is lowercased before comparison but guest emails are compared without lowercasing, so any guest email containing uppercase characters bypasses the blacklist entirely. An operator configures BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=do-not-invite@example.com and an authorized booking attendee submits 'Do-Not-Invite@example.com'; the includes(guest) check fails to match and the blacklisted address is added to the booking and emailed the full event details (location, video call URL/password) — a normalization-mismatch bypass of a security control.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) (logical AND), so a user must be BOTH admin and owner for the flag to be true; a team admin who is not the owner is denied, and the variable name promises OR semantics. Team admins (non-owner) cannot add guests to their team's bookings, silently getting FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission' — the intended authorization path is dead code for admins; also suggests the two calls were meant as alternatives, and any future edit toggling this to || without re-review widens access unexpectedly.

[ADVISORY] The duplicate-attendee check guest === attendee.email is case-sensitive while email equality is conventionally case-insensitive (the blacklist two lines above lowercases, showing the codebase knows this). An attendee who is already 'Alice@Example.com' on the booking can be re-added as 'alice@example.com', creating a duplicate attendee row that then receives two copies of every subsequent email/ICS update; whoever maintains the booking data gets silent drift.

[ADVISORY] The booking lookup uses findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } }) with no userId/organization scoping — authorization is applied only after a fully-loaded fetch of credentials, payment references, and destination calendars for any booking in the database by numeric id. Defense-in-depth relies entirely on the post-fetch check at lines 46-48; any future refactor that touches that check (or an early return before it) turns this into a cross-tenant read of organizer credentials — the tenant scoping should be in the query, not bolted on afterward.

[ADVISORY] The catch block around sendAddGuestsEmails swallows the error with a bare console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") and no error object or telemetry. When the email provider fails, the mutation still returns 'Guests added' success to the user and operators get no diagnostic — guests exist in the DB but were never notified, and the failure is invisible except as an unlogged-in-detail console string in production logs.

[ADVISORY] The organizer is fetched with prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }), so a booking with a null userId (unassigned/team bookings exist in this schema) produces an unhandled Prisma NotFoundError that surfaces as an uncaught 500 rather than a typed TRPCError. Any permitted caller (team owner) adding guests to a booking whose userId is null gets a raw INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with no useful message, and the guest rows may already be created since the update happens after — actually the fetch precedes the write, so the request fails cleanly but as an unhandled exception polluting error telemetry with stack traces.

[ADVISORY] The guest rows are committed to the attendees table before the calendar and email side effects run, with no compensation path, so a failure after the prisma.booking.update leaves the database mutated while the user sees an error. When eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees throws (expired credential, video reference mismatch), the handler rejects, the client shows 'unable_to_add_guests', but the guests are already permanently persisted as booking attendees — the retry re-adds the same guests (or hits the duplicate check with a confusing BAD_REQUEST), and the calendar never gets the update; an operator has no reverse path to clean up the orphaned rows.

[ADVISORY] New guest rows are written to the shared BookingAttendee table with name: "", conflating invited guests with the attendee who booked, and there is no code path anywhere in this diff to remove a guest once written. Every downstream consumer of booking.attendees (cancellation emails, ICS regeneration, booking detail views) now treats guests as full attendees with blank names, and a user who adds a wrong address has no way to undo the write — the data change is effectively irreversible from the product surface, only repairable by direct DB access.

[ADVISORY] The uniqueness check reads booking.attendees from the earlier findFirst and then performs a createMany with no unique constraint enforcement, so two concurrent addGuests calls both pass the filter and both insert the same guest email. A user double-clicking Add (the button's only guard is isPending) or two attendees adding the same guest concurrently produces duplicate attendee rows for one booking, which then feed duplicated entries in the calendar update, emails, and ICS with no dedup or rollback step.

[BUG] The team permission check uses `&&` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, requiring the caller to be BOTH admin and owner. A team admin who is not the owner is denied with FORBIDDEN even though the variable name and intent (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`) say either role should pass; team admins lose the add-guests feature entirely.

[BUG] Blacklisted or already-present guest emails are silently filtered out of `uniqueGuests` while the handler returns success for the remainder. The user submits [a@x.com, b@x.com] where b@x.com is blacklisted; the API returns "Guests added" with no indication that b@x.com was dropped — the organizer believes the guest was invited and that guest silently never receives anything. Silent-partial-success on a user-facing operation.

[BUG] Attendees are committed to the DB via `prisma.booking.update(...createMany)` before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs, and a failure there aborts the request with a raw 500 while the guests remain persisted. When the calendar update fails (bad/stale credential, expired token), the user sees a 500 error, retries, and then hits the "all emails already exist" path from the uniqueGuests filter — the guests exist in the DB but were never added to the calendar event and no email was sent (sendAddGuestsEmails is skipped on throw). Partial write with no rollback on a user-facing operation.

[BUG] The catch around sendAddGuestsEmails logs a static string with console.log and discards the error object, and the handler still returns success. When email delivery fails, the user sees "guests added" success toast, guests appear on the booking, but no notification email ever goes out and no error is recorded — the operator cannot distinguish this from a success in logs either, since `err` is never logged. Invisible failure of a user-facing operation.

[ADVISORY] `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws a raw Prisma NotFoundError (unhandled, non-TRPC) when booking.userId is null. A booking with a null userId produces an unhandled Prisma error surfaced as a 500 instead of a TRPC 4xx, and the error message/stack shape leaks the internal query failure into the tRPC error chain; the FORBIDDEN check above never runs because it is only reached... it does run, but a null-user booking passes the isAttendee branch for attendee callers and then crashes.

[BUG] The toast fallback is dead code: `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` is a template literal that is always truthy (at minimum `"undefined: undefined"`), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` never shows the fallback. When err.data or err.message is missing (network error, non-TRPC failure), the user sees the literal string "undefined: undefined" instead of the intended "Unable to add guests" message — a never-rendering fallback that also fails open to garbage content.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails branches on the raw `newGuests` (original request input) rather than the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so it misclassifies which attendees are the new guests. When a blacklisted or already-present email is submitted alongside new guests, those non-added addresses still influence the branch; more importantly the new guests themselves (who are now booking attendees) match `newGuests.includes(...)` and receive the full AttendeeScheduledEmail while pre-existing guests get AttendeeAddGuestsEmail — an invited guest gets a "your event has been scheduled" email and existing guests get the change notice, inverting the intended notification semantics when mixed lists are submitted.

[ADVISORY] `isInvalidEmail` is only cleared by the Cancel button; a successful validation->mutation after a prior invalid attempt leaves the red "Emails must be unique and valid" banner visible over the success flow. A user who fixes the invalid emails and clicks Add sees the success toast, dialog closes, but on reopening the dialog the stale error state (never reset on success or dialog open) — actually state persists per component instance — shows the error banner while the form is now valid, misdirecting the user to think their input is still invalid.

[ADVISORY] The `guests` array has no `.max()` cap, so the handler accepts an unbounded email list and fans it out into unbounded DB inserts, per-attendee translation fetches, N×M email sends, and calendar attendee updates on a request path. A single authenticated caller can submit thousands of emails, causing thousands of BookingAttendee rows and thousands of outbound emails plus a calendar API call with that attendee list (which the provider will reject at some size), turning one request into a mass-mailing/outbound amplification primitive; retries after the calendar reject re-trigger the fan-out since only exact-duplicate emails are filtered.

[ADVISORY] replyTo is built as `[organizer.email, ...all attendees' emails]` with no bound, growing with booking size; also `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` crashes on an empty attendees array. For bookings with many attendees the replyTo list grows unboundedly until SMTP receivers reject the header (hard send failure for the organizer notification); and since sendAddGuestsEmails uses Promise.all, one rejection rejects the whole send — combined with the swallowed catch in the handler, all guest notifications fail silently. The attendees[0] access is safe in practice because the organizer email is separate, but the subject construction throws a TypeError if attendees is empty.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `isInvalidEmail` is only cleared by the Cancel button; a successful validation->mutation after a prior invalid attempt leaves the red "Emails must be unique and valid" banner visible over the success flow. A user who fixes the invalid emails and clicks Add sees the success toast, dialog closes, but on reopening the dialog the stale error state (never reset on success or dialog open) — actually state persists per component instance — shows the error banner while the form is now valid, misdirecting the user to think their input is still invalid.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed `safeParse`, but it is not cleared on a later successful submit or in the mutation `onSuccess` handler (which only closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`). Since the dialog component remains mounted in `BookingListItem` and only `open` toggles, the `isInvalidEmail` state persists across closes/reopens, causing the red "Emails must be unique and valid" banner to remain visible even after a successful add and on subsequent opens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `guests` array has no `.max()` cap, so the handler accepts an unbounded email list and fans it out into unbounded DB inserts, per-attendee translation fetches, N×M email sends, and calendar attendee updates on a request path. A single authenticated caller can submit thousands of emails, causing thousands of BookingAttendee rows and thousands of outbound emails plus a calendar API call with that attendee list (which the provider will reject at some size), turning one request into a mass-mailing/outbound amplification primitive; retries after the calendar reject re-trigger the fan-out since only exact-duplicate emails are filtered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new authenticated `addGuests` mutation whose input schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts`) accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no size limit. The handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) then (1) creates many attendee rows via `createMany` for each provided email, (2) runs per-attendee translation fetches (`Promise.all(attendeesListPromises)`), (3) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with the full attendee list, and (4) sends emails to organizer/team members and every attendee via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. This makes a single request able to trigger unbounded DB writes + outbound email fan-out + a potentially huge calendar provider update, matching the finding’s amplification concern. No `.max()`/rate limiting is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] replyTo is built as `[organizer.email, ...all attendees' emails]` with no bound, growing with booking size; also `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` crashes on an empty attendees array. For bookings with many attendees the replyTo list grows unboundedly until SMTP receivers reject the header (hard send failure for the organizer notification); and since sendAddGuestsEmails uses Promise.all, one rejection rejects the whole send — combined with the swallowed catch in the handler, all guest notifications fail silently. The attendees[0] access is safe in practice because the organizer email is separate, but the subject construction throws a TypeError if attendees is empty.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce the cited patterns: in `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, `replyTo` is constructed as `[this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]` with no cap, and the `subject` uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`, which would throw if `attendees` were empty. Also `sendAddGuestsEmails` awaits `Promise.all(emailsToSend)`, and the handler wraps it in a `try/catch` that only logs, so a rejection is swallowed. However, the claim that this will *definitely* cause SMTP hard failures (and that *all* notifications fail) is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone; it’s an important robustness/edge-case concern grounded in the new code rather than a proven, always-reproducible defect.
